key_rulings.C1: Fix shape is a GUARD around the line-326 EndNonUndoableTask() call, NOT the reorder the issue prose proposed. P-5 proved usm.Save() itself raises 'Commit at wrong place.' at CurrentDepth > 0 and collapses the envelope, so swapping lines 326/332 trades one guaranteed raise for another with no save either way.
key_rulings.C6: P1 is a hard PREREQUISITE of P0: the guard checks depth first and only calls EndNonUndoableTask() when an envelope is open, then still wraps the call so any other raise cannot skip Save().
key_rulings.C9: Q1 RECONCILED. The owner's incident is a P-5 -> P-3 CHAIN: mid-session SaveChanges() under undoable=False hits usm.Save() at depth 1, raises the owner's exact 'Commit at wrong place.' string and collapses the envelope; the collapsed envelope then makes CloseProject()'s unguarded End raise, skipping Save(), losing the whole in-memory session. The C6 guard breaks the chain. The trigger is reachable from flexicon's own SHIPPED SaveChanges() docstring Example (FLExProject.py:563-588), correct under undoable=True and a guaranteed raise under undoable=False -- so no owner repro steps were needed.
key_rulings.C10: The .fwdata file-swap detail is OUT OF SCOPE and must not be claimed as fixed. CloseProject() has no path that renames/rotates/replaces .fwdata; the probe's delta-0 result is the correct consequence of Save() never running. Attributed to FieldWorks-side recovery, left unexplained by design.
key_rulings.C11: HasOpenSessionTask() reads depth BEFORE the self._undoable mode check. The cycle-2 dispatch brief's 'return False WITHOUT consulting depth' wording was WRONG and is superseded. Two independent reasons: (1) C4 requires closed/never-opened to raise FP_ProjectError from BOTH members with no mode carve-out -- short-circuiting first would make a closed undoable=True project answer False instead of raising, the exact silent-answer ambiguity P1 removes; (2) FLExProject has no __init__ and OpenProject() assigns self.project (line ~263) BEFORE self._undoable (line 271), so on a never-opened instance testing self._undoable first raises a bare AttributeError instead of the documented FP_ProjectError. C3 is NOT weakened: depth is read for its raise-or-not effect only and discarded unread on the Phase 2 branch, so the ANSWER is still never depth-derived under undoable=True. Do not 'fix' this back to the brief wording; overturning it requires citing C11 explicitly.
key_rulings.C12: T2 DROPPED, not deferred, and not merely on cost. The premise was wrong: _ReadActionHandlerDepth() is deliberately STRICT (raises FP_ProjectError, returns depth verbatim -- C5) while transaction.py:_current_depth / undoable_operation.py:102 / CustomFieldOperations.py:306 are deliberately LENIENT (coerce non-int to 0 so a malformed double degrades to 'treat as outermost'). One implementation cannot serve both contracts; sharing them is a conflation, not a de-duplication. Escape hatch 1 (isinstance(depth,int) after delegation) REJECTED: behaviour-preserving in production but it makes the doubles stop testing what they claim to, and decisively the prescribed except-wrapper would swallow the FP_ProjectError the helper exists to raise and substitute 0 -- at CustomFieldOperations.py:306 that silently disables the issue-#21 corruption guard. Escape hatch 2 (edit the static source-grep test at tests/test_custom_field_create_refusal.py:54-60) REJECTED: it deliberately pins that corruption guard's implementation; loosening it for a zero-functional-delta refactor is net-negative, and parking the literals in a comment would be gaming it. Escape hatch 3 (add spec= to the doubles) REJECTED as a means to T2 and NOT owed as a follow-up, since T2 itself is dropped. C5's 'optionally at the implementer's discretion during T2' clause is now CLOSED as declined. Nothing in P0/P1/P2 depends on T2.
key_rulings.C13: What the T4 P-5 measurement DOES and DOES NOT establish. T3's guard is CONFIRMED CORRECT and needs no rework; C1/C6/C7 stand. FROZEN: (1) the rival 'the guard skipped an End that should have run' hypothesis -- which would implicate the fix SHAPE -- is DISPROVED by measurement in the same run: the probe force-calls EndNonUndoableTask() manually before CloseProject() and that forced call STILL raises 'Cannot end task that has not been started.', so the envelope was genuinely gone and an End could not have succeeded either way; (2) black box, live: after a failed mid-session SaveChanges() at depth 1, CloseProject() reaches usm.Save() at depth 0, does NOT raise, and 0/25 persist; (3) therefore usm.Save() RETURNED SUCCESSFULLY HAVING PERSISTED NOTHING -- a sound inference (the usm.Save() call is bare, so a raise would have propagated) but NOT a direct measurement, and it rests on (2)'s 'did not raise' which T4 recorded in prose but never asserted; T6/P-9 must pin it. NOT FROZEN, do not cite as settled: 'the UnitOfWorkService cannot commit after a failed CheckReadyForCommit'. That is a liblcm-INTERNALS claim inferred from one black-box survivor count. Three rival mechanisms produce identical observations: (i) the UOW/UndoStack is poisoned session-wide; (ii) SaveChanges()'s failure path DISCARDED the pending change set, so the loss already happened before CloseProject() was entered and NO CloseProject()-side change could ever reach 25/25; (iii) collapsing the envelope unregistered the dirty objects so usm.Save() correctly flushed an empty change set. Distinguishing (ii) is decisive for #243's ceiling -- routed to T6, not into the contract. Bearing on the user's ruling: all three mechanisms imply the SAME shape for the fourth ask (make SaveChanges() refuse usm.Save() at CurrentDepth > 0), so the uncertainty does not block the decision to approve -- it only bounds what #243 may claim without it.
